candidates.title: Make AI-written code easier to review

demandEvidence.chore: Make code produced with AI understandable enough for a builder to review before shipping.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: That means you can end up with systems you've built where you don't truly understand how all the code works.

ease.reason: A pasted sample can define a small test, but no attached source documents an implementation method.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: an ecommerce operator using AI-written code might value review help; this post does not establish a buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could explain a short synthetic code sample, but reliable coverage and real repositories are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A draft explanation can repeat on supplied snippets; a developer must verify meaning and decide whether code ships.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly describes not understanding built code, but gives no frequency, workflow details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: A proposed explainer could turn operator-selected code into a plain-language outline and questions for review. The discussion states the concern but does not describe a repeat frequency or customer; the assigned ecommerce segment also does not establish a fitting buyer. A proposed small experiment is feasible only with a pasted, non-sensitive sample; no attached implementation reference supports code analysis. A person must verify every explanation before shipping.

candidates.title: Prepare a repeatable chatbot evaluation checklist

demandEvidence.chore: Evaluate an existing document-based assistant, retrieval pipeline or chatbot.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’m looking for firsthand experiences from people who hired someone to evaluate an existing document-based assistant, retrieval pipeline, or chatbot.

ease.reason: A checklist on fictional questions is a modest start, but no attached source documents evaluation tooling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional-services teams commissioning assistant evaluations may value a repeatable checklist; payment for this proposed service is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare a small synthetic question set and format findings; evaluation standards and access are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: Formatting results can repeat, while an evaluator must judge answer quality and source support.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly asks about hiring an evaluator for existing assistants, but does not establish frequency or implementation capability.

candidates.reason: The post asks for firsthand accounts of hiring an independent evaluation of an existing assistant. A narrow proposed mock could take a test question set and produce a checklist of answer, source support and failure notes; those fields are design choices, not source facts. No attached implementation reference supports evaluation mechanics. Use fictional test records; an evaluator must judge correctness and any real deployment needs permission, access and privacy review.

demandEvidence.chore: Count open support tickets and identify how many are urgent.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Can your native n8n workflow count the open tickets, then find how many of those are urgent?

ease.reason: A synthetic ticket table is a small test, but no attached source documents ticket parsing or urgency rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: support teams may value a ticket summary, but this challenge does not establish a buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can count and flag synthetic rows; real ticket access and urgency definitions are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: Counting can repeat on supplied rows, but a person must validate urgency and handle tickets.

evidence.reason: The challenge states the exact count-and-urgency task, but not recurrence, operational rules or implementation support.

candidates.reason: A narrow proposed mock could accept a list of test tickets, count them, and flag urgency for review; urgency rules and fields would be design choices. This overlaps the recent post “A small AI support inbox loop” (e20bcacf021524725d3fc275): both target support teams and automate support-ticket handling. No attached reference supports ticket access or urgency classification. A person must validate flags.

candidates.title: Send a triggered email through Make

demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A test inbox and one trigger define a manageable experiment, though no attached source documents the integration steps.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a business needing triggered email setup might pay for help; this request establishes neither a buyer nor willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use a controlled inbox and sample trigger; provider setup and error cases remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: A test message could send after a trigger, but an operator must approve recipients and troubleshoot delivery.

evidence.reason: The request names the intended SMTP email action and trigger, but supplies no repeated use, successful result or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: A proposed test could use a sample trigger and send a non-consequential email to an operator-controlled test inbox. The request names Make, an SMTP provider and a trigger, but gives no configuration or error-handling details. No attached implementation reference documents this integration. A human must verify recipient, message and permissions before any real send; the source does not show the workflow succeeded.
